questions.prompt: Where can you view, edit, or delete what Claude remembers about you?
questions.explanation: Memory is saved as individual topics you can read, edit (pencil icon), or delete in Settings > Memory. You can also ask Claude to remember or forget things.

questions.prompt: Which kinds of data does memory never save, even on request? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Government ID numbers, criminal history, financial account numbers, and immigration status are never saved. Communication preferences are a normal memory category.

questions.prompt: Custom styles were migrated into ____, which arrive disabled so you can turn on the ones you want.
questions.explanation: Styles moved to skills: custom styles were migrated to disabled skills, most presets were retired, and Learning remains as a skill.

questions.prompt: Match each personalization tool to where it applies.
questions.explanation: Account-wide instructions apply everywhere, project instructions within a project, skills load on demand, and memory accumulates over time.

questions.prompt: Is memory on by default for Team and Enterprise members?

options.text: No. An owner must enable it, and each member opts in
Memory doesn't exist on those plans

questions.explanation: Memory is on by default for Free, Pro, and Max. On Team and Enterprise, owners enable it for the organization and it's off for each member until they opt in.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to keep one client's details out of every other chat.

items.text: Turn off Use account memory on that project for full separation
Create a dedicated project for the client
Periodically review that project's memory and files
Add the client's files and instructions to that project

questions.explanation: Each project has its own memory; turning off account memory gives full separation, and periodic review keeps it clean.
